mechanism_narrative: Sustained decline in RETAIL_REC over four consecutive weeks (-9.4, -13.9, -19.4, -23.0) reflects an accelerating downward trend that will persist into the next four weeks due to inertia in consumer avoidance behavior, producing continued negative RETAIL_REC.
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, or the week-on-week decline rate reverses to positive for two consecutive weeks within the forecast window.

mechanism_narrative: Collapse in TRANSIT mobility (-52.3 to -61.9 percent) signals severe restrictions or behavioral avoidance of public transport. This suppresses retail access via transit-dependent routes, driving RETAIL_REC further negative as commuting infrastructure remains unavailable.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -50 percent for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -61.6 in most recent week
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility recovers above -40 percent within the next two weeks and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises, or RETAIL_REC decline decelerates despite TRANSIT remaining below -50 percent.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has partially recovered from -58.1 to -33.0 percent over two weeks, signaling policy-driven reopening of office capacity. This recovery in workplace commuting will drive retail footfall recovery as workers resume in-person routines and discretionary shopping near employment centers.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 15 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -58.1 to -33.0 between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility falls below -40 percent in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC remains negative despite WORKPLACES recovery continuing above -35 percent.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains elevated (1.1 to 9.9 percent) while RETAIL_REC collapses, indicating consumers are substituting discretionary retail with essential-goods shopping. If GROCERY_PHARM sustains above baseline while RETAIL_REC stays depressed, essential-shopping dominance will suppress retail recovery.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 0 percent and RETAIL_REC below -20 percent simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:divergence between positive GROCERY_PHARM and negative RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -15 percent while GROCERY_PHARM falls below 0 percent, indicating substitution reversal and retail recovery.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has oscillated sharply (-19.3, +12.0, -11.3, -15.9), indicating weather or seasonal policy shifts affecting outdoor activity. Negative PARKS in the most recent week signals deteriorating conditions or restrictions that will suppress outdoor-adjacent retail (e.g., recreation goods, outdoor dining) over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -15.9 in most recent week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility recovers above 0 percent within one week and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises, or RETAIL_REC decline continues despite PARKS recovery.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen from 5.9 to 12.3 percent over four weeks, indicating sustained home-confinement behavior. Elevated residential time combined with depressed RETAIL_REC suggests consumers are avoiding retail environments; this behavioral lock-in will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC negative unless RESIDENTIAL begins declining sharply.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 10 percent for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 5.9 to 12.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 5 percent within the next two weeks and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -10 percent.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in WORKPLACES and PARKS mobility (WORKPLACES +25.1 points from t-2w to t-0w, PARKS oscillating) signals regime shift toward reopening. When both workplace and outdoor activity recover simultaneously, retail footfall follows as consumers resume integrated mobility patterns combining work, recreation, and shopping.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -35 percent AND PARKS rises above -5 percent in the same week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES or PARKS falls below trigger thresholds in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC remains below -15 percent despite both proxies meeting recovery conditions.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT collapse (-61.6 percent) combined with WORKPLACES partial recovery (-33.0 percent) indicates policy-driven shift toward remote work and private transport. This regime change will suppress retail recovery because private-vehicle commuting bypasses retail clusters served by transit, and remote workers reduce discretionary shopping frequency.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -55 percent AND WORKPLACES above -40 percent simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:divergence between transit collapse and workplace partial recovery
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -40 percent within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -15 percent despite TRANSIT remaining below -55 percent and WORKPLACES above -40 percent.
